searches.query: What exact cash compensation will I receive because my lantern battery swelled?

chunks.text: Check the condition, return window, gift status, and transport restrictions separately. A lantern that contains a lithium battery still follows the battery shipping rules. The recipient of an eligible gift return receives store credit under the gift policy; allocation does not change that credit into a bank-card refund. Original shipping fees and a purchased return label remain separate from these item amounts.

Swollen, leaking, or damaged rechargeable batteries  Stop using or charging a rechargeable device if its battery swells, leaks, or is visibly damaged. Do not send it through the ordinary returns process. The store's regular ground return label is not an approved way to ship a damaged battery. Contact the product safety team through the support form and choose the battery-safety category.  Provide the product model, purchase reference, a description of the damage, and photographs when it is safe to take them. The team gives the customer instructions for the specific product and location. Support agents must not improvise a packaging method or tell customers to remove a swollen battery. Follow the device manufacturer's safety instructions while waiting for the team.  The general shipping article permits certain undamaged battery products to travel by ground. That permission does not apply to a damaged battery. Whether the item qualifies for a warranty remedy is assessed separately from how it can be handled safely.

Refund allocation for discounted bundles  When a bundle has one discounted purchase price, allocate that price across its items in proportion to their individual prices at the time of purchase. Refunding one eligible item returns that allocated paid amount. It does not return the item's current price or its undiscounted original price. Retaining other items does not by itself cancel the allocation.  The camping starter kit contains a lantern listed at USD 30, a stove listed at USD 50, and a carry case listed at USD 20. Their individual prices total USD 100. When the customer paid USD 80 for the kit, the allocated paid amounts are USD 24 for the lantern, USD 40 for the stove, and USD 16 for the case. These amounts total the USD 80 actually paid.  The allocation determines money, not return eligibility. Check the condition, return window, gift status, and transport restrictions separately.

Tracking events come from the carrier after dispatch. Return transport for a device with a swollen, leaking, or damaged battery follows the damaged-battery procedure rather than the ordinary parcel-return process. Customers must not mail such a battery using an ordinary return label.

Items containing an undamaged lithium battery must use the eligible ground service. A damaged, swollen, or leaking battery must never be sent using this ordinary label; use the damaged-battery procedure. Label creation does not count as dispatch. The parcel must actually be handed to the carrier within the return's dispatch deadline.

Delivery restrictions for rechargeable products  Products containing lithium batteries travel by ground service within the contiguous United States. The rule covers rechargeable lanterns, headlamps, power banks, and navigation devices, including products whose batteries are installed inside the equipment. These products cannot be sent by our air services, to Alaska or Hawaii, or to an international destination.  Selecting express shipping at checkout does not override this restriction. If a mixed order includes an ordinary item and a rechargeable device, the rechargeable item still travels by ground. A support agent must not promise that paying the express surcharge makes a battery shipment eligible for air transport. The customer can remove the battery product and place a separate order for the other items if those items qualify for the requested service.  Ground shipping has the delivery estimate shown at checkout for the destination. This policy does not supply a guaranteed arrival date for a particular parcel. Tracking events come from the carrier after dispatch.

Published repair charges  The repair workshop offers a tent pole-section replacement for USD 18 per section and a sleeping-bag zipper-slider replacement for USD 25. These prices cover the named repair work only. Any transport charge is stated in the individual quotation. Other repairs, including a torn tent floor, require a quote after assessment. There is no published flat price for a tent-floor replacement.  A manufacturing fault approved under warranty is handled under the product's warranty terms rather than automatically charged as a paid repair. An accidental tear or wear outside the warranty can still be assessed for paid repair. The workshop tells the customer the scope and price before work begins. The customer must approve the quotation; sending an item for assessment is not approval for an unspecified charge.  Active members receive priority queue handling but pay the same published repair prices. Priority is not a completion guarantee.

Check the lithium-delivery and oversize-delivery articles before promising this service. A customer cannot pay a surcharge to remove a product restriction. The membership benefit covers qualifying standard delivery only. It does not discount the USD 18 express price or change the cutoff time.

Reporting delivery damage or the wrong product  Report visible transport damage or a wrong product within seven calendar days after delivery. Keep the outer packaging and photograph the label, packing materials, and affected item. The support team compares those details with the shipment record before approving the claim. If the item is unsafe to use, stop using it while the report is assessed.  An approved wrong-product or delivery-damage return receives a prepaid label. The customer does not pay the ordinary USD 7 change-of-mind label fee for that approved return. The team confirms whether a replacement or another remedy will be provided. A report being opened does not prove replacement inventory exists or establish a delivery date for the replacement.  Damage involving a rechargeable battery follows the separate damaged-battery procedure. Do not put a leaking or swollen battery in an ordinary return parcel even when support is investigating delivery damage. A manufacturing defect discovered later follows the product's warranty process.

answer.answer: The exact cash compensation cannot be established from the supplied evidence. The policy states that a swollen battery must not be sent through the ordinary returns process and requires contacting the product safety team for instructions. Whether the item qualifies for a warranty remedy is assessed separately from how it is handled safely, and no specific refund or compensation amounts for damaged batteries are provided in the documents.
